ayahs.1: By the star as it sets—Allah swears by the celestial sign that just as stars guide travellers through the desert, His Messenger guides souls to their true destination.
ayahs.2: Your companion is neither astray nor misguided.
ayahs.3: He does not speak from his own desire.
ayahs.4: It is only revelation sent down to him.
ayahs.5: He was taught by one of mighty power—
ayahs.6: possessing great perfection, who assumed his true form
ayahs.8: then drew near and came closer,
ayahs.9: until he was two bow-lengths away or even nearer.
ayahs.10: Then Allah revealed to His servant what He revealed.
ayahs.11: The heart did not deny what it saw.
ayahs.12: How then can you dispute with him over what he saw?
ayahs.13: He certainly saw him descend a second time
ayahs.14: at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary—
ayahs.15: near which is the Garden of Abode—
ayahs.16: while the Lote Tree was covered by what covered it in heavenly splendour.
ayahs.17: The sight did not swerve, nor did it overstep.
ayahs.18: He certainly saw some of his Rabb's greatest signs.
ayahs.20: and al-'Uzza, and the third, Manat?
ayahs.21: Do you claim sons for yourselves while you assign daughters to Him?
ayahs.22: That is a most unfair division.
ayahs.23: These are only names you and your ancestors invented—names Allah never authorized. They follow nothing but assumption and whatever their nafs desires, though guidance from their Rabb has already come to them.
ayahs.24: Or should every person have whatever intercessors they wish?
ayahs.25: To Allah belongs the dunya and the Akhirah.
ayahs.26: How many noble angels are in the heavens! Their intercession avails nothing until Allah grants permission to whomever He wills and is pleased with.
ayahs.27: Those who have no iman in the Akhirah label the angels with female names.
ayahs.28: They have no knowledge for this. They follow only assumption—and assumption cannot replace truth.
ayahs.29: So turn away from whoever turns away from Our Reminder and desires only the life of this dunya.
ayahs.30: That is the limit of their knowledge. Your Rabb knows best who strayed from His path and who is guided.
ayahs.31: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth, so He may repay evildoers for what they did and reward the doers of good with the finest reward—
ayahs.32: those who avoid major sins and shameful acts except minor lapses. Your Rabb is vast in forgiveness. He knew you best when He produced you from the earth and while you were still fetuses in your mothers' wombs. So do not claim purity for yourselves. He knows best who has taqwa.
ayahs.33: Have you seen the one who turned away,
ayahs.35: Does he possess knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?
ayahs.36: Or was he not informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses
ayahs.37: and of Abraham, who fulfilled his covenant?
ayahs.38: That no soul laden with sin will bear another's burden,
ayahs.39: and that each person will have only what they strove for,
ayahs.40: and that their striving will be seen,
ayahs.41: then they will be fully rewarded,
ayahs.42: and that to your Rabb is the final return.
ayahs.43: And that He is the One who brings joy and grief,
ayahs.44: and gives life and causes death,
ayahs.45: and created the pairs, male and female,
ayahs.46: from a drop of emitted fluid,
ayahs.47: and that upon Him is another creation—resurrection,
ayahs.48: and that He enriches and gives sufficiency,
ayahs.49: and that He is the Rabb of Sirius,
ayahs.50: and that He destroyed the first 'Ad,
ayahs.52: and the people of Noah before them—they were the most unjust and transgressing,
ayahs.53: and He overturned the overturned cities,
ayahs.54: and covered them with what covered them.
ayahs.55: So which of your Rabb's favours will you dispute?
ayahs.56: This is a warner like the warners of old.
ayahs.57: The imminent event has drawn near.
ayahs.58: None besides Allah can avert it.
ayahs.59: Do you marvel at this discourse,
ayahs.62: So prostrate to Allah and worship Him alone.
